question: Why is the Mālinī body ultimately a body of Śakti rather than a mere phoneme arrangement?
premises: Through entry into ritual efficacy, that body becomes a body consisting of Śakti.
In ultimate truth, this Śakti-body arises from the mutual stirring of seeds and wombs.
That stirring is an emissive arising, not a merely mechanical combination.
inference: The Mālinī nyāsa produces a Śakti-body because the phonemic seeds and wombs mutually stir and give rise to emissive power.
uncertainties: The technical sense of 'bīja' and 'yoni' here spans phonemic, mantric, and cosmological registers.
The compound 'vaisargikodayāt' may emphasize visarga-based emission; the verse does not spell out the full mechanism.
plain_english: Because it enters into ritual efficacy, that body is, in ultimate truth, a body of Śakti. It arises from the mutual stirring of the seeds and wombs, through an emissive arising.
